units.function: Real-process tests for Cursor-local runtime credential/prompt injection, optional mode, Skill synchronization and local/remote executable selection.
units.dependencyDirection: Server Vitest -> @paperclipai/adapter-cursor-local execute -> adapter-utils child process/callback bridge -> temporary filesystem and a local runner standing in for remote sandbox; no database, Secret service, authorization, policy enforcement or evidence store.
units.keyDataModels: Run/Agent/company/runtime, Cursor command/cwd/model/mode/env/prompt, PAPERCLIP runtime credential variables, runtime Skills, execution target/remote cwd and process result/session.
units.lifecycle: Prepare prompt/env and global Skill links -> resolve local or remote executable -> optionally start callback bridge -> spawn Cursor with stdin prompt -> parse successful session/result.
units.testAssessment: Sandboxed Vitest passed 3/5 and the two remote cases failed only because callback bridge listen was denied; approved unsandboxed rerun passed 5/5. Tests prove happy-path process wiring but omit every cancellation/timeout/retry/resume/failure/idempotency/approval/evidence case and do not validate actual sandbox isolation or credential scope.
units.designRationale: Give Cursor Agents authenticated access to Paperclip APIs, reusable company Skills and consistent execution across local and sandbox targets with minimal operator configuration.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs least-privilege Connector execution where each Run gets isolated instruction state, scoped short-lived control-plane capability, trusted executable provenance and durable pause/resume/cancel/evidence/result behavior.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT behind the Connector SDK and local execution node. Issue a short-lived Run capability bound to company/Agent/work/contract/action scope; isolate Skills per Run with signed provenance; require allowlisted/attested executables and sandbox policy; implement versioned events, idempotency, pause/resume/cancel/timeout and evidence digests. Retain only the real-process fixture and remote-bridge test pattern.
units.responsibilityConflict: The Agent receives a general Paperclip API credential and instruction that it exists, while no test binds allowed calls to exact work, data/tool grants, approval or accountable human. Shared global Skills can silently alter behavior across responsibility contexts.
evidence: 2026-08-19 sandboxed focused Vitest: 3 passed, 2 callback-listen EPERM failures
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL least-privilege gap: PAPERCLIP_API_KEY is injected and advertised to the Agent with no tested audience, endpoint/capability scope, expiry or exact work/approval binding. HIGH cross-context instruction risk: Skills are symlinked into global ~/.cursor/skills without tenant/Run isolation, provenance, immutable digest, collision or cleanup tests. HIGH supply-chain risk: ~/.local/bin is preferred and arbitrary explicit remote commands are accepted without allowlist/owner/hash/signature attestation. Missing tests cover Secret leakage, hostile Skills, concurrent tenants, bridge token scope, direct network egress, cancellation/kill, timeout/output limits, failure classification and durable evidence.
